action: Government defenders: learn how SoftEther VPN normally behaves on your network and hunt for unexpected SoftEther services; use the IOC list and YARA rules Rapid7 published, and TLS inspection where available.

attribution.note: Rapid7 attributes the tool to Webworm, a China-aligned APT, with moderate confidence

date_note: Date of Rapid7's publication; activity dates are not stated in the post
exec: A China-aligned espionage group is using a rebuilt VPN tool that avoids malware detection, aimed at government networks.
plain: Security firm Rapid7 says a China-aligned spying group called Webworm uses a modified copy of the legitimate SoftEther VPN program to reach government networks without classic malware.

key_findings: Rapid7 describes a custom build of SoftEther VPN Bridge (based on version 4.44, build 9807) rebuilt from source, with renamed branding, changed HTTP endpoints and handshake so stock clients cannot connect.
The resource archive is embedded in the binary and the configuration is stored encrypted with a custom cipher.
Rapid7 attributes the tool to Webworm with moderate confidence, citing TTPs matching ESET's earlier reporting and hosting infrastructure linked to the group before.
Webworm is described as a China-aligned APT focused on governmental organizations, especially in Europe; the post gives no victim counts or country list.
recommendations: Learn SoftEther's normal behaviour on the network, since the actor can easily change endpoints and watermark.
Use Rapid7's published IOC list and YARA rules; detect via TLS inspection where available.

summary: Rapid7 published research on a modified build of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge that it attributes, with moderate confidence, to Webworm, a China-aligned group known for targeting governments, especially in Europe. The build changes branding, endpoints and handshake and encrypts its configuration to evade detection. Rapid7 names no victims.
title: Rapid7: Webworm uses custom SoftEther VPN bridge to spy on governments without malware

validation.note: Single vendor research post by Rapid7, read in full; attribution is Rapid7's own at moderate confidence.

review.note: Compared date, Rapid7 attribution to Webworm at moderate confidence, China-aligned government focus, SoftEther changes, no victims against the Rapid7 post
